title: 3-Read Friday #31: Story Planning, Attention Routines, and Maths Gems
author: Craig Barton
summary: In the 31st installment of 3-Read Friday, Craig Barton spotlights three posts: Jemma Sherwood on using narrative structure to plan sequences of maths lessons, Jody Chan on classroom routines for building and sustaining student attention, and Jo Morgan's latest '5 Maths Gems' resource roundup. Barton frames Sherwood's post as a rare but valuable entry from an infrequent blogger, praising her application of the 'story' metaphor to lesson-sequencing decisions. He connects Chan's piece to what he calls one of his 'obsessions' -- avoiding poor proxies for listening -- and highlights her practical strategies for gaining attention before and during teacher explanations. He closes with an enthusiastic nod to Morgan's gems collection, calling out specific resources on inverse proportion, Pythagoras questions, and prime-factorisation tasks that caught his eye.
points: Barton calls Sherwood's post on planning a mathematical story a rare treat, noting she 'doesn't blog all that often, but when she does, it is a good one.'

He links Chan's attention-routines post directly to his own recurring concern about 'poor proxies for listening,' framing attention-getting as a prerequisite skill teachers must deliberately build, not assume.
He singles out three specific resources from Morgan's gems roundup (inverse proportion, Pythagoras questions, product of prime factors) as personal favourites for 'maths geeks.'
quotes: Jemma doesn’t blog all that often, but when she does, it is a good one. Here, Jemma explains the power of the memorable nature of stories, and then proceeds to describe how we can utilise this power when planning and delivering a sequence of lessons.
If students are not paying attention, they will not learn, and avoiding poor proxies for listening is one of my obsessions at the moment.
Here, Jody shares some practical strategies we can use before and during explanations to help sustain our students’ attention.
The Queen of Resources returns with another lovely selection of maths gems.
I particularly enjoyed Catriona’s take on inverse proportion, Nathan’s set of questions on Pythagoras, and Mr Coward’s product of prime factors task.
